reasoning: The deepseek model successfully audited the PKGBUILD and all patch files it reviewed, finding them to be standard AUR packaging for legitimate Epson scanner software with no malicious indicators. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was due to API errors (HTTP 400), not security concerns. However, both models incorrectly skipped two patch files (0002-Fix-crash.patch and 0003-Use-XDG-open-to-open-the-directory.patch) by misclassifying them as binary files, creating a coverage gap that prevents high confidence.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from the qwen model experiencing API failures when auditing the PKGBUILD and 0006-Fix-crash-no-serial-number.patch files, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully completed the audit of these same files and found them safe. This is not a substantive disagreement about security, but rather a tool failure in one model.
coverage_issues: Both models incorrectly classified 0002-Fix-crash.patch and 0003-Use-XDG-open-to-open-the-directory.patch as binary files and skipped them. These are text-based patch files that should have been reviewed.
The qwen model failed to audit the PKGBUILD and 0006-Fix-crash-no-serial-number.patch due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), leaving critical files unaudited in that report.
false_negatives: The two skipped patch files (0002-Fix-crash.patch and 0003-Use-XDG-open-to-open-the-directory.patch) were not reviewed and could potentially contain malicious code, though this is unlikely given the package context.
learnings: The file classification logic incorrectly identifies .patch files as binary. Patch files are text-based diffs and should always be reviewed. The tool should use file extension or content-type detection to properly classify patch files as text.

When a model encounters API errors during audit, the system should either retry with a different model or clearly flag the incomplete coverage rather than returning an inconclusive verdict that triggers unnecessary escalation.

The audit tool should validate that all files in the AUR repository have been successfully reviewed before returning a final verdict, and should distinguish between 'skipped due to classification' and 'skipped due to error'.
